notes.title: Shipwright's Request
notes.author: Ragnhild Keel-Wright of Windhelm
pages:
To any brave heart passing through.
Old shipwrights in Windhelm say that when Ysgramor buried his son, he set a carving from the prow of Yngol's longship above the tomb, a sea-wolf's head in black oak. They say any new ship blessed by touching it will never founder on the Sea of Ghosts.

I am building a ship for my sons, who fish the ice-floes every spring. My husband was lost off Winterhold. I will not lose them too. Bring me the sea-wolf's head, or let me touch it once, and I will carve your name into the keel. I pay in honest Stormcloak coin.

notes.title: Epitaph of Yngol
pages:
^Rendered from the old runes by a College hand
The sea took my son and gave me nothing back. I give him this hall instead, and the sea-wolf from his ship, and the songs of five hundred.
Let him guard this coast as I could not guard him.

^Beneath it, newer, in a Windhelm hand
Shipwrights come here before every launching, though the old rule says they should not. They touch the stone of the door and ask the son of the Harbinger to keep their keels whole. Some say he answers. Some say the sea answers instead. Both kinds come back.

weynon_stones.hook: A ring of weathered standing stones in the snowfields of the central Pale. Shepherds lead their flocks around it, never through, and nobody remembers why.
weynon_stones.rumour: The Weynon Stones? Just old rocks. But my granda always walked around them widdershins, and my granda lived to ninety.

notes.title: Survey of the Weynon Stones
notes.author: Brynja Stormquill
pages: Waymark 26: Weynon Stones. Nine stones in a broken ring, two fallen. Not Dwemer, not Nordic in any style I know. Older. The lichen on the north faces is thick as a fur.

Curious detail: the snow inside the ring melts a day earlier in spring than the snow outside it. The shepherds say the stones keep a fire under them. I put my ear to the largest stone and heard nothing, then something, then nothing. Recommend a College mage with better ears than mine.

notes.title: Shepherd's Counting Rhyme
pages:
~One for the fallen, two for the cold,
~Three for the lamb that never grew old,
~Four, five, six for the shepherd's lost sons,
~Seven and eight for the wolves and their runs,
~Nine for the stone that hums in the night,
~Walk round the ring and keep it in sight.

^Note from Brynja Stormquill
The shepherds' children skip around the ring singing this, always widdershins, never through. When I asked a girl why, she said, 'Because the ninth stone is listening.' When I asked what it was listening for, she ran away.

shrouded_grove.hook: A misty grove in the snowfields of the central Pale where warm springs keep the trees green through winter. Its spriggans have turned savage, and an old herbalist wants to know why.
shrouded_grove.rumour: The Shrouded Grove stays green in the dead of winter. Pretty, if you don't mind the tree-women watching you from behind the trunks.

notes.title: Herbalist's Journal
notes.author: Liv Moss-Mother
pages:
#5th of Hearthfire
For thirty years I have gathered snowberries and frost mirriam in the Shrouded Grove, and for thirty years the spriggans have let me. I leave them honey; they leave me be. That is the bargain.

#22nd of Hearthfire
The eldest spriggan, the one with the antlers of white birch, attacked me today. Her bark has gone black at the heart, like rot, and her lights are red. Someone has cut into the old tree at the centre of the grove and taken heartwood. A woodcutter's axe-marks. A greedy fool.

#23rd of Hearthfire
The heartwood must be put back, or the elder must be put down. I can do neither. If a kind soul passes, there is honey in the jar by my door.

bronze_water_cave.hook: A cave by a coppery pool east of Nightgate Inn, home to a family of cave bears. The pool takes its colour from Dwemer metal washed down from the ruins above.
bronze_water_cave.rumour: Bronze Water Cave? Bears. Just bears. Lots of bears. The water tastes of pennies, too.

notes.title: Trapper's Notes
notes.author: Aldis of Nightgate
pages: Bronze Water: three bears this season, a sow and two yearlings, plus the old male who comes and goes. Do not set snares near the pool. The bears drink there at dusk and they do not like surprises.

Odd thing: the water is green-bronze because of Dwemer scrap washed down from the Great Lift. I found a cog the size of a shield at the bottom. The College would pay for it, maybe. If I can find a way to drag it out without being eaten.
Going north to the Driftshade hills next week to trap wolves. Better pelts up there.

blizzard_rest.hook: A giant camp on the open snowfields of the Pale, close enough to Heljarchen Hall that the new homesteaders can hear the mammoths grumbling at night.
blizzard_rest.rumour: The giants at Blizzard Rest are calm enough if you leave their mammoths be. The trouble is, somebody hasn't been leaving their mammoths be.

notes.title: Poacher's Contract
notes.author: a Windhelm buyer
pages: Wanted: mammoth tusk, whole, unbroken, at least six feet. Price: two hundred septims per pair, delivered to the back door of the alchemist's in Windhelm. No questions asked. No answers given.

Advice from the buyer: the herd at Blizzard Rest has an old cow with the best ivory in the Pale. The giants are slow in the cold. Strike at dawn, cut fast, run downhill.
^Scrawled beneath in another hand: Erik tried it. Erik is now part of the snowfield.

notes.title: Complaint to the Jarl's Steward
notes.author: Vantus Loreius
pages:
Steward,
Poachers are cutting tusks off the mammoths at Blizzard Rest and the giants are coming down to the road looking for whoever did it. Yesterday one of them sat on my fence. It is no longer a fence.

Hang the poachers or pay for my fence, I do not mind which. Preferably both.
V. Loreius

^Postscript
Also, one of the giants has taken to leaving a mammoth's tooth on my doorstep every morning. I do not know whether this is an apology or a threat. My wife says it is a courtship. I would like the Steward's opinion on all three possibilities, in writing.

pale_stormcloak_camp.hook: A Stormcloak war camp in the eastern Pale, close to the Dwemer ruins and the Windhelm road. Its sergeant is short-tempered, short of men, and short one company banner.
pale_stormcloak_camp.rumour: The Stormcloak camp near Raldbthar is a cheerful place. Well, it was until their banner walked off with one of their own.

notes.title: Company Roster
notes.author: Sergeant Gunnvor Ice-Brow
pages:
Bear-and-Axe Company, the Pale camp.
Present: 22. Wounded: 4. Sick (nightmares, Dawnstar men, useless): 3. Deserted: 1, Kolbeinn Rime-Hand, with the banner. Dead: 0 this month, Talos be thanked.

Supplies: arrows short, mead shorter. The Winter War was meant to bring the arrows to the Winterhold camp and some on to us. No word of her.
Orders from Windhelm: hold the road, watch Fort Dunstad, do not provoke the giants. Sergeant's additional orders: do not provoke the sergeant.

^Added in Gunnvor's hand
Rumour from the Nightgate road says Kolbeinn went into Forsaken Cave. If any of you go after him on your own, you're on latrines until Ulfric is High King.

korvanjund.hook: An ancient Nordic crypt in the central Pale, said to hold the crown of the old High Kings. Soldiers of both sides of the war have been seen scouting its approach.
korvanjund.rumour: Korvanjund's got an old king's crown in it, or so they say. The Legion wants it to keep it from Ulfric. Ulfric wants it to wear. The draugr want everyone to leave.

notes.title: Scout's Dispatch
notes.author: a Legion scout
pages:
To the Commander, Fort Dunstad.
Korvanjund: entrance clear of snow, recently. Fresh tracks, heavy boots, at least a dozen. Somebody is preparing an expedition. I saw a blue sash in the scrub. Stormcloaks, almost certainly.

Shepherds say the crypt was opened in the time of the old kings and resealed with something buried in it that the kings did not want found. They also say the sheep near it come back with frost in their wool in summer. I believe the second part.

notes.title: Lament for the Crowned Head
pages:
~They laid the king beneath the hill,
~And bound his brow with jagged gold,
~And told his sons to wait until
~The crown should rise when Skyrim's old.
~Now Skyrim's old, and sons are many,
~And every son would be a king.
~The hill keeps one, and gives not any,
~And the dead keep counting everything.

^Note on the back of the page
Sung in the alehouses of Dawnstar and Windhelm both, though the last verse changes depending on who is buying. The Windhelm version names Ulfric. The Solitude version names nobody, and the singer looks over his shoulder.

volunruud.hook: A Nordic tomb hidden in the hills of the western Pale, where a rich and nervous stranger has been seen meeting cloaked figures at night.
volunruud.rumour: Somebody's using Volunruud for secret meetings. Fine clothes, soft hands, Imperial accent. You don't go to a draugr tomb to sell a horse.

notes.title: Inscription in the Ceremonial Hall
pages:
^Rendered from the old runes by a College hand
Here sleeps the warrior who would not kneel, and here his axe sleeps apart from him, lest the two of them wake together and remember their old quarrel with the world.
Whoever joins axe to hand, joins the warrior to his anger. Let them make sure their own anger is large enough to hold his.

^Copyist's remark
I have heard that someone has lately been holding meetings among these very carvings. One hopes they are not the sort of people to read old warnings as instructions.

notes.title: Hired Guard's Note
notes.author: a hired guard
pages: We're paid to keep the road clear while the gentleman meets his friends in the crypt. Two hundred septims, and we never see the friends. They come up the back way. The gentleman says nobody speaks of this, ever.

Fine by me. Except Ragnar swears that one of the friends walked right past him in the dark and he never heard a footstep. Ragnar's not right since. Keeps checking behind him. I'm starting to check behind me too.
Last night the gentleman left in a hurry and dropped a scrap of paper with a black hand on it. I burned it. Some things you don't want to be holding when the Jarl's guards come by.

tumble_arch_pass.hook: A natural rock arch over the road in the hills of the eastern Pale, with giants camped beneath it. Travellers must choose between a long detour and a short, loud conversation.
tumble_arch_pass.rumour: Tumble Arch? Giants under it, like trolls under a bridge. You can go round. It takes a day. Most folk take the day.

notes.title: Warning Painted on a Board
notes.author: a Khajiit caravan
pages:
This one writes for the next caravan.
Giants under the arch. They do not like bells. They do not like music. They do not like Ri'saad's cousin, who rang a bell and played music. Ri'saad's cousin is now a little flatter than before.

Go round by Korvanjund, or wait for night when the giants sleep and walk softly. Do not ring bells. Do not be Ri'saad's cousin.
May your road lead you to warm sands.

^Postscript from a second Khajiit
This one adds: the giants also do not like moon sugar. They do not like it when you throw it at them. That one tried. It does not distract them. It only makes them sticky and more angry.

great_lift_at_raldbthar.hook: A Dwemer lift by the ruins of Raldbthar, its brass housing poking out of the snow. Quaestor Vesk believes it is one end of a vast hidden road beneath the Pale.
great_lift_at_raldbthar.rumour: The brass tower near Raldbthar hums at night. College folk come out and listen to it like it's a bard. Strange people, mages.

notes.title: Second Note on the Lifts
notes.author: Quaestor Aurelian Vesk
pages: The lift at Raldbthar hums at a pitch identical, within the limits of my tuning fork, to the lift at Alftand (1). This cannot be coincidence. The Dwemer did not build in coincidences.

(1) My tuning fork is of Dwemer make, purchased in Markarth at ruinous expense. I am told the fence who sold it now lives at Fort Fellhammer. I do not wish to know how he came by it.
Hypothesis: both lifts descend to a single great cavern. Proposal: find it. Precondition: find a brave assistant, now that Brelas is gone.

irkngthand.hook: A great Dwemer city in the southern hills of the Pale, its towers half-hidden by snow. Falmer haunt its lower halls, and someone recently walked in through the front door very quietly.
irkngthand.rumour: Irkngthand. Big Dwemer ruin south of the lift. There's a camp of treasure-hunters near the entrance, and they're nervous about something.

notes.title: Treasure-Hunter's Journal
notes.author: Saeta the Bold
pages:
#Frostfall
We made it into the upper halls of Irkngthand. Gold leaf on the walls, brass in every corner. Then the Falmer. We pulled back to the camp outside the gate.

#Two days later
Somebody else is inside. We heard them on the high walkways, three or four, quiet as cats. Not Falmer, they're too quick and they talk. Thieves, if I'm any judge.
We will wait until they come out and see what they carry. Or we will wait until they come out and pretend we never saw them. Depends on how big they are.

notes.title: Marginal Note on Irkngthand
notes.author: Quaestor Aurelian Vesk
pages: Irkngthand is by some distance the largest Dwemer site in the north, and the worst studied. Its upper halls contain a lens-and-mirror gallery for which I would give my second-best robe and my toe (the other one).

Unhappily the halls also contain Falmer in great numbers, and the College refuses to fund an escort. I am told the Thieves Guild of Riften has an interest in the site. I suggest the College ask the Guild for a map. I am told this suggestion is 'unseemly'.

shearpoint.hook: A jagged peak in the hills of the southern Pale, crowned by a dragon wall and haunted by a masked priest of the old cult who never truly died.
shearpoint.rumour: Shearpoint's a dragon roost. And not just a dragon. There's a masked thing up there, floating, that the dragon seems to bow to.

notes.title: Climber's Journal
notes.author: Ottar Hook-Hand
pages:
#Frostfall
I have climbed every peak between Whiterun and the sea and Shearpoint is the last. A dragon circles it on fine days; on foul days it doesn't, so I'll climb on a foul day.

#Later
Reached the wall at the summit. A figure in robes and a carved mask, hovering a hand's breadth above the snow, turned to look at me. I said good morning. It raised its staff and the air went cold enough to crack my teeth.
I ran. I'm writing this in a crevice below the summit. My hands are blue. I left my best ice-axe up there. Somebody please fetch it for me.

raldbthar.hook: A Dwemer ruin in the southern Pale, its halls still guarded by brass constructs. Quaestor Vesk of the College has staked his reputation on what lies inside.
raldbthar.rumour: Raldbthar. Bandits camp in the upper halls, Dwemer machines guard the lower ones. Either way, you'll be fighting somebody's property.

notes.title: Commission from Quaestor Vesk
notes.author: Quaestor Aurelian Vesk
pages:
Commission for any competent person (1).
In the lower halls of Raldbthar there is a chamber containing a tonal regulator: a brass rod fixed in a cradle of struts, which hums when touched. I require it, intact, at the College of Winterhold. My fee is generous and my gratitude is, I am told, tiresome.

(1) Competence is defined as: able to tell a Dwemer sphere from a Dwemer chamber-pot, and able to run away from the former.
Beware the bandits in the upper halls; they are not interested in scholarship. Beware the centurion in the lower; it is not interested in anything at all.

notes.title: Bandit's Complaint
pages: We took this ruin because it was warm. Nobody said the warm came from the machines. Nobody said the machines would wake up when Gorm kicked the brass spider. Gorm's dead. The brass spider is fine.
Rule from now on: nobody goes below the third stair. Nobody kicks anything. Nobody listens to that mage who keeps sending letters about rods.

Second rule: the warm part of the ruin is ours, the clicking part belongs to the machines, and the scholar can come and have his rod if he wants it so badly. Third rule: if the scholar sends a sellsword instead, we hide. Gorm didn't hide. Look how that turned out.

hillgrunds_tomb.hook: The barrow of Hillgrund, a chieftain of the Merethic Era, at the southern edge of the Pale above the Valtheim road. His descendants still come here, and lately they have stopped coming back.
hillgrunds_tomb.rumour: Hillgrund's Tomb. The old chief's family still buries their dead there. Old Hillgrund doesn't seem to like the company.

notes.title: Letter from a Descendant
notes.author: Ingrun Hillgrund-Kin
pages:
Cousin Torvar,
You went into the tomb to lay Grandfather's urn with the rest of the line, and you never came back. Our family has done this for twenty generations. Not once has the old chief stirred. Now the guards at Valtheim say they hear iron dragging inside the hill at night.

Grandmother says the old chief's horn was taken from his bier by a grave-robber last summer, and that he will not rest until it is returned. I do not believe in such things. I also do not go near the hill anymore.
If you are alive, come home. If you are not, I hope someone sets the horn back where it belongs.

notes.title: Grave-Robber's Scrawl
pages: Took a drinking horn off the old chief's slab. Silver rim, carved with ravens. Worth a hundred to the right buyer at Darkshade. Got as far as the door and the whole tomb woke up behind me.

Hid the horn in the side passage and holed up here. They keep walking past. The big one keeps stopping at the passage and smelling the air. If I put it back, maybe they'll let me go. If I put it back, I'm poor again.

the_tower_stone.hook: An ancient standing stone on the frozen Winterhold coast, carved with the sign of the Tower. Those who touch it are said to find locks yielding and doors opening for them.
the_tower_stone.rumour: The Tower Stone gives you a knack for getting into places. Thieves swear by it. So do jailers' wives, and that's a whole other story.

notes.title: Thief's Thanks, Wedged in a Crack
notes.author: a grateful burglar
pages:
Stone of the Tower,
Last year I touched you and the next three locks in Windhelm opened like flowers. Then the fourth one opened onto the guard captain's bedroom, with the guard captain in it. I am writing this from the road to Dawnstar, which is where I live now.
I am grateful, but next time could you be more particular about which doors you open? I leave you a lockpick, bent, in thanks. It is the last one I have.

the_serpent_stone.hook: A standing stone on a lonely ice floe off the eastern Winterhold coast, marked with the sign of the Serpent. Reaching it means crossing the ice, which is a test in itself.
the_serpent_stone.rumour: The Serpent Stone's out on the ice. You get there by jumping floe to floe with the slaughterfish watching. It gives you a sting in your fingers, they say. Worth it? Ask the fish.

notes.title: Verse Carved in the Ice Beside the Stone
pages:
~The Serpent wanders through the sky,
~It has no house, it has no throne,
~It bites the stars and passes by,
~And leaves its venom in the stone.
^Carved below by another hand: I crossed six floes to read this. It does not rhyme as well as I hoped. Still, my hands are tingling.

^Below that, scratched in the ice and already half-melted
Three floes south, the slaughterfish wait. They always wait. Cross quickly and do not stop to admire the view, however fine it is in the dawn light.

notes.title: Apprentice's Field Note
notes.author: Novice Faldrus Hlervu
pages: Field note for Master Tolfdir's class on standing stones. The Serpent Stone is the most isolated of the thirteen. It stands on a floe that has not drifted in living memory, though every floe around it does.
I touched it. My fingertips went numb and then very hot, and for an hour afterward anything I touched felt like a beehive. Recommend gloves. Recommend not falling in on the way back, which I did.

Master Tolfdir says the sting of the Serpent is the Stone's blessing: a venom in the fingertips that the bearer may cast on a foe. I believe him. I accidentally cast it on a mudcrab and the mudcrab has not forgiven me.

dragon_mound_pale_imperial_camp.hook: An ancient dragon burial mound near the Legion camp on the western Pale coast. It steams in the frost, and the soldiers have stopped joking about it.
dragon_mound_pale_imperial_camp.rumour: The mound south of the Legion camp has been steaming like a kettle. Old graves don't steam. Not unless something under them is warm.

notes.title: Picket Report
notes.author: Decurion Marcia Tellus
pages:
To Quartermaster Ostorian.
Night picket at the old mound. Third night running it has steamed in the frost. Last night two figures in old Nord armour stood on the top of it until dawn, facing the sky, motionless. When the sun came up they walked down into the ground. Through it, I mean.
The men are frightened. I am not frightened, sir. I am merely recommending that somebody with more experience of the dead than a Legion picket look at it before something comes out of it with wings.
